description: Entity-level git merge driver. Resolves false conflicts git invents when independent agents edit the same file. ~95% reduction vs. line-based merge.
vibe: Merge at the entity, not the line — and make every refusal explain itself.
highlights: Entity-level merge semantics: conflicts are resolved at function/class granularity, so independent edits to different functions never collide.
Conflict markers carry a machine-readable 'refused_by:' line naming the guard and quoting the exact disputed lines — the failure mode is self-diagnosing.
weave check always emits a verdict sentence (OK/FOUND), never a bare empty result, and exits 0/1 so it composes with hooks and scripts.
Explicit honesty about limits: 38 languages supported, but .vue/.svelte/.erb/.hs fall back to git because weave 'does not yet merge well enough to claim'.
WEAVE_EVENT=1 emits one JSON line per merge (including failures) so 'which files conflicted, on what, and how long' is a single pass, not four stderr channels joined by hand.
assessment: This is a rare case of a tool whose interface is designed around its own failure modes: the conflict marker tells you why it refused, weave explain narrows the blast radius, and weave check verifies the human's fix against the three merge stages. The refusal to overclaim — falling back to git for formats it can parse but not merge well — is the kind of taste that builds trust in a merge driver, where a silent wrong answer is worse than a loud conflict. The event stream and exit-code discipline show the author thinks about weave as a component in a pipeline, not just a CLI.
